gist: Pompliano argues Bitcoin likely bottomed after a ~50% drawdown from $125k to ~$60k, citing near-record hash rate, ~135k BTC bought via perpetual preferreds plus ~800k in ETFs, and Q4/midterm seasonality, and predicts year-end gains for both BTC and equities while framing AI as offense and Bitcoin as defense. Much of the episode is a critique of Anthropic's IPO governance (Long-Term Benefit Trust, public-benefit share plan) alongside praise for its business; the title's 'regret' is his 2021 laser-eyes episode.

insights.claim: Pompliano argues loud 'Bitcoin is going to zero' calls from people like Jason Calacanis and Chamath Palihapitiya create a dislocation between narrative and fundamentals that conviction investors can exploit for asymmetric returns.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Bearish consensus from prominent voices is treated as a contrarian buy signal.
insights.quote: We need two sides to the market.

insights.claim: Bitcoin hash rate is back to near all-time highs despite many large miners converting to HPC/AI data centers, which Pompliano frames as Bitcoin being backed by computing power, the world's most valuable commodity.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Network security is recovering even as miner capacity migrates to AI, undercutting the 'miners abandon Bitcoin' bear case.
insights.quote: hash rate is back to almost all-time highs

insights.claim: Pompliano says perpetual preferreds from Strategy, Strive and others, citing Fidelity research, have bought over 135,000 BTC, adding to roughly 800,000 BTC in ETFs for almost a million BTC removed from the market, with Strive buying about 5,000-6,000 BTC in the last week.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Perpetual preferred issuance is a new structural net buyer of Bitcoin, similar to ETFs.
insights.quote: I think there's over 135,000 Bitcoin that have been purchased as part of the perpetual preferreds.

insights.claim: Bitcoin fell from about $125k to roughly $60k (a ~50% drawdown) with a violent capitulation that usually marks a bear-market bottom, and has since recovered, which Pompliano reads as confirmation the bear market is likely over with ~50% upside back to all-time highs.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Frames current $80-85k levels as early-recovery with defined upside to prior highs.
insights.quote: It had this very violent puke, which usually marks the bottom of a bear market

insights.claim: Pompliano predicts both equities and Bitcoin will end the year higher than current levels because Q4 is seasonally strong, especially in midterm years, and midterm uncertainty will resolve into renewed capital inflows.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Positions for a post-midterm year-end rally in risk assets.
insights.quote: we're going to end the year higher than where we are right now in both of those markets

insights.claim: Pompliano thinks Bitcoin goes to $1 million at some point but not next year.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Long-term target without near-term timeline.
insights.quote: I think Bitcoin goes to a million at some point. I just don't think it's going to happen next year

insights.claim: Pompliano's public company has been selling Bitcoin at NAV to buy back shares, which he describes as increasing Bitcoin exposure per shareholder.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Treasury companies trading near NAV are using buybacks as an accretive lever.
insights.quote: We've been selling Bitcoin at NAV and buying back shares

themes.theme: Bitcoin as defense, AI as offense

insights.claim: Pompliano now splits new capital roughly 50/50 between Bitcoin and AI rather than 100% Bitcoin, framing AI as offense and Bitcoin as defense amid capital rotation into AI.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Even Bitcoin maximalist-adjacent allocators are rotating part of flows toward AI.
insights.quote: I look at AI is offense, Bitcoin is defense.

insights.claim: Pompliano says Bitcoin's cycle returns are compressing: $1k to $20k in 2017, down 85% to $3k, up to $69k, down to $15-16k, then up to $125k.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Expect lower but still above-market cycle returns.
insights.quote: The returns are compressing.

insights.claim: Pompliano argues Bitcoin is the least risky it has been in years due to Lindy effect, hash rate, adoption, Wall Street financialization and regulatory clarity, so it should return less, maybe 30% a year compounded vs 10-15% for stocks.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Lower risk implies lower but still index-beating expected returns.
insights.quote: maybe it goes up 30% a year now on a compounded basis

insights.claim: Pompliano argues AI is an abundance technology bringing abundance of dollars, intelligence and information, so scarce assets (Bitcoin, gold, productive land, scarce collectibles) become more valuable as SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI succeed.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Positions AI success as a tailwind, not a competitor, for hard assets.
insights.quote: In a world of abundance, scarcity becomes more valuable.

insights.claim: Asked about Bitget CEO Grace Chen's claim that Bitcoin could swing 30% either way as big AI IPOs hit, Pompliano agrees there has been significant capital rotation toward AI but says volatility can work in both directions.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Large AI IPOs are a potential liquidity event for crypto.

insights.claim: Pompliano says Anthropic appears to have burned less than $10 billion to reach what may be $75-100 billion of annual revenue, an incredible business if accurate, though it faces headwinds from self-owned intelligence, fine-tuning, personal agents and model routers.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: If S-1-derived estimates hold, capital efficiency is exceptional, but commoditization pressures are real.
insights.quote: they burned less than 10 billion dollars to generate what looks like it could be somewhere between 75 to 100 billion dollars of annual revenue

insights.claim: Pompliano says Anthropic's plan to put some percentage of the company into a public-benefit vehicle it controls looks like power accumulation, and challenges it to give shares directly to children via Invest America accounts as Michael Dell and Elon Musk did.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Governance structures tied to 'public benefit' may be a red flag for IPO investors.
insights.quote: that sounds a lot like power accumulation to me

insights.claim: The co-host highlights that Buddy Shah, named on page 145 of Anthropic's S-1, chairs the Long-Term Benefit Trust that can appoint and remove any portion of Anthropic's board while holding no stock and being off payroll.
insights.speaker: Co-host (readtheprofile.com writer)
insights.so_what: Board control sits with a non-equity trust, an unusual governance risk for public shareholders.
insights.quote: He is not on payroll. He does not own stock.

insights.claim: Pompliano argues independent directors should have equity skin in the game and calls the trust's no-equity independence 'smoke and mirrors'.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Investor skepticism of the Long-Term Benefit Trust could weigh on IPO sentiment.
insights.quote: It's all smoke and mirrors.

insights.claim: Pompliano says the US government ripped Anthropic out and contracted with competitors after Anthropic restricted how the government could use its software, calling it market forces at work.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Use restrictions can cost AI vendors government revenue to less restrictive rivals.
insights.quote: The government said, "No. Kick rocks.

insights.claim: Despite governance criticism, Pompliano says he pays for and uses Anthropic's products, calls Claude and Opus excellent technology, and suggests listeners may consider buying the IPO while separating product from the moralizing.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Product quality and governance concerns are separable in the IPO decision.
insights.quote: I think that it's a fantastic product.

insights.claim: Pompliano says Elon Musk's timelines are meant to be hit about 50% of the time, which is why SpaceX and Tesla draw criticism despite reusable rockets, Starlink and Optimus.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Discount Musk timelines rather than dismissing the companies.
insights.quote: he expects it to be hit 50% of the time

insights.claim: Pompliano calls putting laser eyes on his Twitter profile near the end of the 2021 bull market, at an influential person's request, one of his biggest Bitcoin regrets because tying identity to an asset blinds clear thinking.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Tribal identity in an asset is a warning sign near cycle tops.
insights.quote: maybe the laser eyes blind you

insights.claim: Pompliano frames 'Bitcoin psychosis' and 'AI psychosis' as extreme versions of valid theses, saying he buys 30-40% of the maximalist vision but rejects claims like holding cash violates Bitcoin's ethos.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Be an optimist without going crazy; keep cash and diversification.
insights.quote: clear eyes, no lasers

insights.claim: Pompliano contrasts AI-skeptical New York users, who hesitate to connect accounts and data, with San Francisco users who hook everything up, a dynamic Silvia considers in product design.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Regional trust differences affect AI agent adoption.
